frequency_question: How often do congressional resolutions of disapproval successfully pass both chambers and survive or override a presidential veto?
membership_rule: Includes all formal joint resolutions of disapproval introduced against major international arms sales and nuclear agreements since the enactment of the AECA (1976) and AEA review provisions, where a vote was forced. Excludes informal expressions of disapproval or resolutions that failed to reach a floor vote.
window: 1976 to present (covering 50 years of statutory review mechanisms)
provenance_note: rate of 0% from only 5 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 5 major historical legislative veto / joint resolution challenges; all 5 failed to achieve the necessary two-thirds majorities in both chambers to overcome executive resistance.
known_gaps: Does not include instances where the executive withdrew or modified agreements prior to a formal vote due to anticipated congressional friction.
skeleton: Statutory review cases under AECA/AEA where a formal privileged motion forced floor action in both chambers.
multiplier: 5 historical challenges resulting in 0 successful veto-proof overrides of foreign policy agreements.
validity_reason: Statutory frameworks governing nuclear cooperation agreements (Section 123 of the Atomic Energy Act) and legislative veto procedures remain stable unless Congress fundamentally alters the AECA/AEA statutory review clocks.
